pages.title: The digital plate record
text: **The durable representation of an observed plate**

The digital plate record is the foundation of the proposed simulation system. It stores observations, identity, timing, calibration, handling events and reviewer decisions. A record can be valuable without a predictive model: it allows a laboratory to revisit what was observed and to understand how a reported measurement was produced.
## What belongs in the record

Each acquisition should retain its original file, a content integrity value, device configuration and the time interval over which the signal was acquired. Measurements derived from an image should link to that image and to the calibration and algorithm versions used. A corrected boundary becomes a new measurement event associated with the reviewer and reason.

The record should distinguish physical identity, direct observations, derived measurements, qualified interpretations and simulations. These layers answer different questions: which object was observed, what was recorded, what analysis calculated, what the reviewed workflow concluded and what a model estimates beyond observation.
## Preservation is a product capability

The stored record should remain intelligible if the original instrument is replaced or a model is retired. This requires documented formats, units, reference identifiers and an export path. Retaining only a screenshot of a final result would lose information needed for investigation and reanalysis.

The record does not become a predictive twin merely because it contains many sensors or a three-dimensional visualization. Prediction requires an explicit model, a defined question and evidence that the model can answer that question within a stated domain. Those additional requirements are developed throughout this part.

pages.title: From record to computational model
text: **A model turns a question into a calculation**

A computational model represents selected features of a physical system using mathematical rules or learned relationships. It may describe an optical measurement, the expansion of a colony or the distribution of an antimicrobial in a medium. Its scope should follow the question; a detailed rendering of an enclosure does not necessarily improve a biological forecast.
## Define the quantity of interest

For AMReye.AI research, candidate quantities include visible colony area, a spatial growth probability, a time to a defined observation threshold or a forecast distribution of an image-derived measurement. These quantities differ from susceptibility categories and require separate validation before any clinical interpretation is considered.

The same image may support several models, but each needs a separate output identity. An estimated biomass should not be relabelled as a measured viable count. A model can fit the observed past while being unsuitable for extrapolation, particularly when multiple parameter combinations explain the same early trajectory.
## Start with a baseline

A constant-value forecast or a simple growth curve establishes whether a more complex model adds information. Complexity should be justified by improved predictive performance, useful uncertainty and practical interpretability. The proposed platform should preserve baseline results alongside experimental models during development, making improvement testable rather than assumed.

pages.title: Requirements for a predictive twin
text: **A predictive twin must remain connected to evidence**

The proposed predictive twin is a computational representation linked to a particular physical plate, updated when qualified observations arrive and used to answer a bounded forecasting question. A general probabilistic twin framework has been demonstrated in engineering research; transferring that idea to microbiological plates requires new biological evidence. [R59]
## Minimum functional contract

The twin should identify its physical counterpart, current model version, last accepted observation, estimated state and permitted prediction horizon. It should also describe the conditions under which updating is suspended. An image rejected for identity or calibration failure should not automatically adjust the biological state.
## Bidirectional use needs an additional gate

A twin might eventually recommend a further observation or a virtual experiment. Any action that changes the physical assay, such as adjusting incubation or exposure, needs its own validation and control path. A simulation service should not gain authority over an instrument simply because the two exchange data.

Reader V1 can establish the record and measurement foundations before a predictive twin is available. This sequence supports future research while keeping the initial product proposition credible. The twin's maturity should be assessed by its validated forecasting domain, not the number of simulated images it can generate or the visual realism of its interface.

pages.title: A state space view of plate development
text: **State evolution and observation are different processes**

A state-space formulation separates biological development from the process used to observe it. Let xₖ represent the latent state at time tₖ, uₖ the recorded inputs and θ the model parameters. A proposed discrete representation is:
**xₖ₊₁ = f(xₖ, uₖ, Δtₖ; θ) + wₖ**
**yₖ = h(xₖ, cₖ) + vₖ**

Here yₖ is an observation, cₖ describes calibration or capture conditions, wₖ represents unresolved process variation and vₖ represents observation error. The equations are a modelling scaffold, not an implemented AMReye.AI algorithm. Vector components may have different units and therefore need explicit scaling and covariance definitions.
## Choose interpretable states where possible

A simple research state might contain visible occupied area and a growth-rate parameter. A richer state could represent local population density, nutrient availability or antimicrobial concentration. Including an unobservable state adds assumptions; it does not make that quantity measured.

State variables must remain within their defined ranges. Missing temperature intervals cannot be assumed constant without an explicit assumption. Segmented area in mm² retains image and segmentation uncertainty. Process variation should describe unresolved biological changes rather than absorb every instrument defect.

The model should use actual elapsed time, especially when acquisition intervals vary. Numerical propagation over a long gap may require smaller internal steps than the observation interval. Testing should challenge irregular timing, abrupt input changes and boundary conditions before the representation is used to support forecasts.

pages.title: Observation models and sensor likelihoods
text: **The observation model connects biology to a sensor**

An observation likelihood describes the probability of obtaining a signal for a given model state and capture condition. This connection is essential because cameras, gas sensors and electrical probes measure different physical effects. Their outputs should not be treated as interchangeable estimates of bacterial abundance.
## Examples of observation relationships

For an image, a forward model may include illumination, object geometry, optical blur, sampling and sensor noise. A simplified model might instead relate segmented area to a latent occupancy state. For a gas channel, the relationship may additionally depend on chamber mixing, background atmosphere and transport delay.
## Avoid double counting

Two features extracted from the same image often share errors. Treating them as independent can produce an unjustifiably narrow posterior distribution. A model should account for shared image quality, calibration and preprocessing where these materially affect the output.

Observation models need calibration data that distinguish sensor behavior from biological variation. A stable optical target can help assess image formation, while it cannot establish the relation between image appearance and viability. The proposed system should retain both types of evidence and identify which relationship each experiment actually tests.

pages.title: Time origins and biological age
text: **Clock time is not automatically biological age**

A forecast needs an explicit time origin. Specimen collection, inoculation, antimicrobial exposure, incubation entry and first image are different events. A trajectory indexed only by file creation time can conceal a long and variable period of biological development before the first observation.
## Proposed temporal record

Each event should carry a timestamp, time zone or UTC representation, precision and provenance. Device clocks also need a synchronization status. If an operator enters an approximate time, the record should preserve that approximation rather than displaying false second-level precision.
## Timing uncertainty propagates

In a rapidly changing phase, uncertainty about when growth began may dominate uncertainty about an image-derived area. A model fitted to a single early image cannot always distinguish a larger initial population from a longer unobserved growth period. The resulting ambiguity should widen the forecast or limit the permitted question.

For a sub-two-hour research target, the clock origin must be stated before evaluation. Reporting time from first image when the intended claim concerns specimen-to-result time would omit preparation and prior incubation. The platform should preserve multiple workflow intervals so that speed can be assessed honestly for each intended use, including unsuccessful and delayed cases.

pages.title: Spatial representations of plate growth
text: **Represent the spatial feature that matters**

Plate growth can be represented as a continuous field, a grid of local measurements, a set of segmented objects or a graph of tracked colonies. These representations trade spatial detail against data requirements and computational cost. A whole-plate average can conceal a small localized event that matters to heteroresistance research.
## Candidate representations

An occupancy map describes where visible growth is present. An object representation records individual boundaries, locations and tracking identities. A radial profile can summarize an approximately circular inhibition pattern, but its validity decreases when the boundary is irregular or neighboring zones interact.
## Coordinate systems are part of the evidence

Spatial observations should refer to a plate coordinate system with units and a transform from image coordinates. Registration uncertainty should accompany comparisons across time. If the plate rotates or shifts, a stationary pixel does not represent a stationary biological location.

The proposed model should retain access to original images even when a reduced representation is used for computation. A reviewer may need to inspect a location excluded by the segmentation. Spatial compression should therefore be evaluated against the intended research question, including rare local features, rather than judged only by average reconstruction quality.

pages.title: Population growth model families
text: **Growth curves are hypotheses with domains**

Population models provide compact descriptions of change. An exponential model, dN/dt = μN, represents growth at a constant specific rate μ. A logistic form, dN/dt = μN(1 − N/K), adds a limiting level K. These equations are illustrative mathematical baselines; neither automatically describes the visible area, viability or antimicrobial response of a real plate.
## Map the variable before fitting

If N denotes cell number, its units and measurement basis differ from a normalized image intensity. An image-derived proxy may have a nonlinear relationship to population size, especially after objects overlap or the detector saturates. Fitting the same equation to different proxies does not give the fitted parameters the same biological meaning.
## Early agreement can hide later divergence

Several curves may fit the first observations almost equally well but imply very different later behavior. A one-day record therefore does not establish that the remaining days can be reconstructed reliably. The useful forecast horizon depends on the organism, assay, conditions and output.

The research programme should compare model families prospectively on withheld future observations. Reporting only goodness of fit to the observed past would not test forecasting. Parameters should retain uncertainty and correlation, particularly when the observed period covers only a small part of the proposed growth trajectory.

text: **Transport models connect location, time and exposure**
Spatial antimicrobial exposure can be explored with transport equations. An illustrative reaction–diffusion form is:

Here c is concentration, D is an effective diffusion coefficient and r represents a specified loss or reaction term. If distance is expressed in mm and time in hours, D has units mm²/h. The equation is a research starting point, not a calibrated disk-diffusion model for AMReye.AI.
## Boundary and initial conditions matter

A simulation requires a description of the initial distribution and the behavior at the domain boundaries. Disk release, agar properties, geometry and environmental history may influence the modeled exposure. A visually plausible gradient is insufficient evidence that the concentration field is correct.
## Do not reverse a clinical method casually

An observed zone diameter does not uniquely identify the underlying concentration history or a minimum inhibitory concentration. Different parameter combinations can produce similar visible boundaries. Inferring an MIC from a simulated field is therefore a separate research claim requiring a suitable reference method and validation.

A useful first application may be sensitivity analysis: determining which uncertain transport assumptions most affect a proposed observation schedule. Such a study can inform experiment design without claiming that the simulation replaces an established susceptibility method.

pages.title: Mechanistic and learned hybrid models
text: **Hybrid models combine constraints and learned relationships**

A hybrid model uses mechanistic structure for some processes and learned components for others. For example, a transport calculation might describe a spatial input while a learned observation model relates local state to image features. Another design could use a simple growth equation with a bounded, data-driven residual term.
## Define responsibility at each boundary

The mechanistic component should declare its assumptions and parameter units. The learned component should declare its training domain and output constraints. Their combined uncertainty is not necessarily the sum of two independent errors, because the components may have been fitted to the same data.
## Preserve meaningful constraints

Nonnegative quantities, bounded occupancy and causal timing can be enforced where the underlying definition requires them. Constraints reduce some implausible behavior but do not prove that the model is biologically correct. A perfectly smooth, nonnegative trajectory can still make an inaccurate forecast.

Evaluation should compare the hybrid with both its mechanistic baseline and a suitable purely empirical model. The comparison needs held-out conditions and an explicit computational cost measure. A more elaborate model is justified when it offers a demonstrated advantage for the intended question, such as better calibrated forecasts or useful transfer with limited data, while preserving an intelligible route for investigating failure.
